text:
Maya: Heads-up — I pushed a first pass of telemetry surfaces for continuous batching. Goal: make it obvious when kernel selection or kv-cache patterns cause low utilization.

Maya: Key panels I added: batch_utilization_pct, avg_batch_size_by_model, queue_depth_p50/p95, tokens_processed_per_sec, kernel_switch_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, microbatch_wait_time_ms.

Sanjay: nice. what sampling rate are you using? we need to keep ingestion cost < 0.2% of infra spend.

Maya: currently 5% on production traffic + 100% on shadowed traffic for 2 canaries. we can lower to 1% if cost spikes.

Leo: can you paste the prometheus queries? i'd like to wire an alert for "avg_batch_size < 2 for > 5m while queue_depth > 3"

Maya: sure — pasted below. these are rough, will refine.

```
# avg batch size (per model)
avg_over_time(redwood_batcher_avg_batch_size{env="prod"}[5m])

# batch utilization
100 * avg_over_time(redwood_batcher_tokens_served / redwood_batcher_capacity_tokens[5m])

# tokens/sec
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_processed_total[1m])) by (model)

# kernel switches (count of runtime kernel selection events)
sum(rate(redwood_runtime_kernel_switch_total[1m])) by (kernel, model)

# kv cache hit rate
(sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))) * 100
```

Olga: small nit — for kernel_switch_count we should tag by sequence_length_bucket and device_type so we can correlate long sequences with fallback kernels.

Maya: good call. added those labels to the metric.

infra-bot: ALERT: perf-regression-detector detected a 12% drop in batch_utilization_pct for model="redwood-v1" between 2051123200 and 2051123300. See: https://perf.redwood/internal/alerts/PR-4321 :boom:

Sanjay: saw the alert. is that correlating with a kernel rollout or with KV cache thrash?

Maya: initial profile indicates kernel latency spiked on cuda-matmul path; kv hit rate held steady. attaching a flamegraph link and the pprof snapshot. https://artifacts.redwood/profiles/2051123300/flame.html

Leo: For the dashboard layout I propose 3 rows: 1) global health (util%, tokens/sec, queue depth), 2) per-model breakdown (avg batch size, kv hit rate, kernel switches), 3) deep diagnostics (pprof links, recent traces, sample request IDs). Also add small sparklines for trend.

Maya: sounds good. i also added a "fallback rate" single stat (percent of requests that dropped to cheaper model variant) — useful when autoscaler triggers fallback and util changes.

Devex: can someone write a 2–3 sentence blurb for the docs / changelog explaining the new charts and suggested runbooks for when util dips? i'll include it in the next release notes.

Maya: draft for devex below, feel free to edit:
"Continuous Batcher telemetry: new dashboard surfaces batch utilization, queue depth, token throughput, kernel selection events, and KV cache hit rates. Use the top-level red/yellow thresholds to detect regressions; when batch_utilization drops while queue_depth rises, check kernel_switch_count and the flamegraph link to identify costly kernels. If fallback_rate increases, inspect recent routing policies and model variants."

Sanjay: also adding a short-runbook: if util < 40% AND queue_depth > 5 for 5m -> capture pprof, enable conservative batching (increase batch window by 10ms), and revert recent kernel changes.

Olga: gRPC probe to grab a sample request for debugging (useful in runbook):

```
grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","prompt":"trace me"}' api.redwood.internal:8080 redwood.InferenceService.GetSample
```

Maya: one last ask — before we ship, run the dashboard with 24h retention in staging and a 1% sample in prod for 48h. we'll evaluate cost vs signal and then move to 5% if useful.

infra-bot: NOTE: nightly cadence job will auto-collect pprof snapshots when batch_utilization_pct < 30% for > 15m.

Leo: thanks all. i'll mock the dashboard tiles and post a screenshot in #eng-runtime tomorrow. :eyes:

Maya: thanks — leaving this thread open for follow-ups. feel free to ping me directly for access to the pprof artifacts.
